request.outcome: Avoid cutting a prose meta description in the middle of a word.
request.status_reason: This 2014 report was imported in 2015, has no comments, and its current deployment/applicability is not established. Open status alone cannot qualify it as a live unmet need.

requirements.text: Do not split a description word at the truncation boundary.
requirements.quote: meta description does not truncate on word boundaries

environment: HTML meta description containing prose; runtime/version not established.
missing_information: Policy when a first word is longer than the budget.
Whether the old report still applies.
Plain-text conversion and HTML escaping contract.

matches.summary: Reuse the lower-level smart_truncate mechanism without the slug product's normalization; strict whole-word behavior needs an edge-policy adapter.

checks.reason: With word_boundary=True and save_order=True it can keep ordinary space-separated words in order. However, no separator or no fitting first word falls back to a hard slice (lines 87-88 and 100-101), so the unconditional requirement is NOT satisfied by the helper alone.

obstacles: The default save_order=False can skip early words; opt in explicitly.
Unknown budget/runtime and old demand; no qualified opportunity or proven extraction.
Do not pass raw HTML or call slugify on prose.

bridge.summary: Inspect smart_truncate independently and resolve oversized-word policy before adopting it.
steps: Prepare plain text and establish the real length budget from the target application.
Test ordinary words, an oversized first word, no-space text and multi-byte characters in an isolated environment.
Compare ordinary slicing versus smart_truncate on the same text and budget, measuring whole-word/prefix preservation.
Define an explicit empty-result/over-budget policy for edge cases, and HTML-escape only after truncation.
bridge.existing_contribution: The separately exported low-level word-selection mechanism; the slug normalization pipeline is not used.
bridge.new_logic: Length budget, target HTML integration and oversized-word policy remain to be specified; none are claimed implemented.
assumptions: 160 characters is illustrative, NOT a request-derived requirement.
Space-separated prose only for this example; grapheme-aware and pixel-aware truncation are not established.
